excerpt: I was working on some experimental physics... I changed my Ph.D. area to machine learning... I was really [needing to learn] coding. It got hours and hours... She [the supervisor] was always supported me... step by step.
analysis: Describes a fundamental career shift from a hypothesis-driven, experimental science domain to a data-intensive, iterative AI/ML domain. Highlights the learning curve and need for support in transitioning to a new technical paradigm.

excerpt: I was working on astronomical time series data... It was hard to find an algorithm that... address this question for all 14 classes... I had to choose one algorithm, but it was not... It underestimates some of the classes... I accept to not rightly estimate this kind of stars.
analysis: Illustrates the tension between the ideal of a universally accurate model (data-centric AI knowledge) and the practical reality where algorithmic choices force trade-offs, accepting failure on certain classes—a clash with the domain expectation of comprehensive understanding.

excerpt: In my academy in Turkey, I see that they're so bored, they do not want to give me time... At Johns Hopkins... they were treating us equally and whenever I want... time they gave me time.
analysis: Contrasts a traditional academic environment (described as disengaged/resistant to providing time) with a more supportive, data-science-focused institute. This hints at cultural friction against the collaborative, iterative needs of AI work.

excerpt: I faced model bias... I accept to not rightly estimate this kind of stars.
analysis: Acknowledges a model's failure (bias) against certain data classes. The phrase 'I accept' suggests a pragmatic, automation-driven compromise that inherently conflicts with the ethical ideal of fair and accurate representation for all categories.

excerpt: For open source project... She [a lead] left the project for one month and tried to get turn back without any explanation... The problem is that [she was] not qualified to lead... I felt discriminated... We lost so many people in that project.
analysis: Describes project collapse due to leadership failure in an open-source, collaborative AI environment. Highlights how linear project management expectations (consistent leadership) are brittle when applied to dynamic, volunteer-based AI projects. Also touches on the unmet need for competent oversight (reconfigured role).

excerpt: I was stuck... for 3 weeks... just one line [of code]. I couldn't see it... talking with different peoples in different countries... They say Chinese, Germany, India... help me to overcome this problem.
analysis: Demonstrates a positive instance where a persistent, non-linear technical problem (a 'bug') was solved through cross-cultural, cross-functional collaboration. This breaks down the silo of working alone or within a single team/culture.

excerpt: In my culture... I'm seeing like a crazy woman... they find this different... as a woman they do not like to hear about so much from you about coding... I feel so supported in multicultural environments.
analysis: Directly contrasts experienced cultural resistance (and gender bias) in a traditional setting against the support found in diverse, international teams. This resistance acts as a hurdle to the role transition into a technical AI contributor.
metaphor: crazy woman (metaphor for deviation from expected role)

excerpt: Incorrect beliefs about different cultures will finish [diminish].
analysis: Expresses an aspirational view that multicultural collaboration in AI work inherently challenges and breaks down cultural stereotypes and misconceptions, leading to more integrated teams.
